title: The Corner Shop
story: Jamal has run a small grocery shop in Mirpur, Dhaka, for twenty years. His daughter Sadia helps him after college and has started taking online orders, which Nabil delivers on his motorbike. Rahima, a loyal customer, shops there every week, but a new supermarket has just opened down the road.
storyBn: জামাল বিশ বছর ধরে ঢাকার মিরপুরে একটি ছোট মুদি দোকান চালান। তার মেয়ে সাদিয়া কলেজের পর তাকে সাহায্য করে এবং অনলাইনে অর্ডার নেওয়া শুরু করেছে, যা নাবিল মোটরসাইকেলে পৌঁছে দেয়। নিয়মিত ক্রেতা রহিমা প্রতি সপ্তাহে সেখানে কেনাকাটা করেন, কিন্তু রাস্তার একটু সামনেই সম্প্রতি একটি নতুন সুপারশপ খুলেছে।

units.focus: Talk about changes in the shop and recent events
units.focusBn: দোকানের পরিবর্তন ও সাম্প্রতিক ঘটনা নিয়ে কথা বলা

sessions.tipBn: অতীতে শুরু হয়ে এখনও চলছে বা সদ্য ঘটেছে এমন কাজে have বা has-এর পরে verb-এর past participle বসে।

items.en: Jamal has run this grocery shop in Mirpur for twenty years.
The price of rice has gone up three times since January.
Sadia has just started taking orders through social media.
A new supermarket has opened just down the road.
Rahima has bought her groceries here since her children were small.
More customers have started paying with mobile wallets this year.

sessions.pattern: Subject + haven't/hasn't/has never + past participle (+ yet) ...
sessions.tipBn: না-বোধক করতে have বা has-এর পরে not বা never বসে; yet সাধারণত বাক্যের শেষে থাকে।

items.en: Jamal hasn't raised the price of eggs yet.
The supplier has not delivered the cooking oil this week.
Sadia has never given a customer the wrong change.
Rahima hasn't gone back to the new supermarket since her first visit.
Business hasn't been this slow since the supermarket opened.
Nabil hasn't missed a single delivery this month.

sessions.tipBn: প্রশ্ন করতে Have বা Has শুরুতে বসে; প্রশ্নে ever ও yet বেশি ব্যবহৃত হয়।

items.en: Have you ever ordered fresh vegetables online from a local shop?
Has the supplier sent the new price list yet?
Has Rahima paid off her bill for last month's groceries?
Has the new supermarket taken away many of your customers?
Have you checked the expiry date on this milk?
Has Nabil delivered the order to the third floor yet?

sessions.tipBn: Wh-শব্দের পরে have বা has, তারপর subject আর past participle বসে; How long দিয়ে সময়ের দৈর্ঘ্য জানতে চাওয়া হয়।

items.en: How long have you owned this shop, Jamal?
Why has the price of onions gone up again?
What has Sadia changed since she started helping her father?
How many online orders have you received today?
Where have you put the receipts from this morning?
Which brand of rice has sold best this month?

sessions.pattern: A short text in the present perfect
sessions.tipBn: অনুচ্ছেদে present perfect দিয়ে এখন পর্যন্ত ঘটা পরিবর্তন ও অভিজ্ঞতা বলা হয়।

items.title: Twenty years behind the counter
items.en: Jamal has worked behind the same counter for twenty years. He has seen prices rise and fall many times, and he has watched his neighbors' children grow up. Many families have trusted him with their monthly shopping. Now he has started to worry about the new supermarket.

items.title: Sadia's new idea
items.en: Sadia has turned the shop's social media page into a small online store. She has posted photos of every product and has listed the prices clearly. So far, more than fifty families have ordered from her. Her father has finally admitted that home delivery is the future.

items.title: A loyal customer
items.en: Rahima has shopped at Jamal's shop for fifteen years. She has tried the new supermarket once, but she hasn't been back since. She has noticed that Jamal's vegetables are fresher and his prices haven't changed much. Most of all, she has always enjoyed a friendly chat at the counter.

units.focus: Describe what was happening when something happened in the shop
units.focusBn: দোকানে কোনো ঘটনা ঘটার সময় কী চলছিল তা বর্ণনা করা

sessions.tipBn: অতীতে চলছিল এমন কাজে was বা were-এর পরে verb-ing বসে; মাঝপথে ঘটা ঘটনা when দিয়ে past simple-এ বলা হয়।

items.en: Jamal was counting the cash when the power went out.
While Sadia was packing an order, three customers walked in.
Rahima was choosing tomatoes while her grandson was playing outside.
Nabil was riding his motorbike to Pallabi when the customer canceled.
The supplier's truck was blocking the road all morning.
People were rushing to buy sugar before the price went up.

sessions.tipBn: was বা were-এর পরে not বসিয়ে অতীতের চলমান কাজকে না-বোধক করা হয়।

items.en: Jamal wasn't paying attention when a boy took a packet of biscuits.
The card machine wasn't working when the evening rush started.
Sadia wasn't answering calls because she was serving customers.
We weren't expecting so many orders on a rainy Tuesday.
Rahima wasn't carrying enough cash, so she paid by mobile wallet.
Nabil wasn't riding carefully when he dropped the eggs.

sessions.tipBn: প্রশ্ন করতে Was বা Were শুরুতে বসে, তারপর subject আর verb-ing আসে।

items.en: Was Sadia checking the stock when the supplier arrived?
Were customers complaining about the prices last month?
Was Nabil waiting outside when you came down?
Were you talking to the supplier when I called?
Was Rahima buying rice when she dropped her purse?
Were you standing in line when the cashier closed the counter?

sessions.tipBn: Wh-শব্দের পরে was বা were, তারপর subject আর verb-ing বসে।

items.en: What were you doing when the power went out?
Why was the customer shouting at the cashier?
Who was minding the shop while Jamal was at the mosque?
Where was Nabil going when his motorbike broke down?
How much were onions selling for in the market last week?
Which products were people buying most before the strike?

sessions.pattern: A short text in the past continuous
sessions.tipBn: অনুচ্ছেদে past continuous দিয়ে ঘটনার পটভূমি আর past simple দিয়ে হঠাৎ ঘটা ঘটনা বলা হয়।

items.title: The power cut
items.en: It was a busy Friday evening. Jamal was weighing lentils, Sadia was packing two online orders, and several customers were waiting at the counter. Suddenly the lights went out. While everyone was looking for their phones, Rahima calmly lit a candle and kept the line in order.

items.title: A late delivery
items.en: Nabil was riding through heavy traffic with six orders in his bag. It was raining hard, and the roads were flooding. While he was waiting at a signal, a customer called and asked where her rice was. He was trying his best, but he arrived forty minutes late.

items.title: At the new supermarket
items.en: Last month Rahima was walking past the new supermarket, so she went inside. Music was playing, and staff in blue uniforms were stacking the shelves. She was comparing two brands of oil when a young cashier offered her a loyalty card. She took it, but she was missing Jamal's friendly smile.

units.focus: Give advice and rules for smart shopping and running the shop
units.focusBn: বুদ্ধিমানের মতো কেনাকাটা ও দোকান চালানোর পরামর্শ ও নিয়ম

sessions.tipBn: উপদেশে should, বাধ্যবাধকতায় must বা have to, সম্ভাবনায় might বা could, অনুমতিতে may বসে; এরপর verb মূল রূপে থাকে।

items.en: You should always check the expiry date before you buy milk.
Customers must show the receipt to return or exchange an item.
We might need to raise the price of sugar next month.
Sadia has to deliver all the morning orders before 11 o'clock.
You could save a lot by buying rice in bulk.
Customers may pay by cash, card or mobile wallet.

sessions.pattern: Subject + shouldn't/must not/don't have to/might not/can't + verb (base) ...
sessions.tipBn: must not মানে নিষেধ, কিন্তু don't have to মানে দরকার নেই; অন্য মোডালের পরে সরাসরি not বসে।

items.en: You shouldn't buy fish if the eyes look cloudy.
Customers must not open packets before they pay.
Rahima doesn't have to pay now because she has a monthly account.
We might not get fresh eggs until Thursday.
You don't need to come to the shop because we deliver.
Nabil can't carry more than ten bags on his motorbike.

sessions.pattern: Should/May/Could + subject + verb ...? / Do + subject + have to/need to + verb ...?
sessions.tipBn: মোডাল প্রশ্নে মোডালটি শুরুতে বসে; have to ও need to-এর প্রশ্নে শুরুতে Do বা Does লাগে।

items.en: Should we offer free delivery for orders above 1000 taka?
Do I have to show my receipt to exchange this?
May I pay part of the bill now and the rest later?
Could you deliver the order to my office instead?
Should I buy the family pack to save money?
Do we need to order more cooking oil before Eid?

sessions.pattern: Statement with a modal, + opposite tag (shouldn't we? / should we?)
sessions.tipBn: হ্যাঁ-বোধক বাক্যের শেষে না-বোধক ট্যাগ আর না-বোধক বাক্যের শেষে হ্যাঁ-বোধক ট্যাগ বসে।

items.en: We should give our loyal customers a discount, shouldn't we?
We must lock the shutter before we go home, mustn't we?
Nabil could deliver the Pallabi orders first, couldn't he?
We shouldn't keep expired products on the shelves, should we?
Sadia needs to reply to these messages quickly, doesn't she?
You don't have to pay for delivery, do you?

sessions.pattern: A short text with modal verbs
sessions.tipBn: অনুচ্ছেদে should, must, have to, might ইত্যাদি দিয়ে পরামর্শ, নিয়ম ও সম্ভাবনা বলা হয়।

items.title: Sadia's shopping tips
items.en: Before you go shopping, you should make a list and set a budget. You don't have to buy everything on the first shelf you see. You might find the same product cheaper in a smaller shop. Most importantly, you must check the expiry date on anything you eat.

items.title: Rules for the delivery rider
items.en: Nabil has to follow a few simple rules. He must call the customer before he arrives, and he should never leave an order outside a locked door. If a customer pays by cash, he needs to count the money in front of them. He may keep any tips he receives.

items.title: Can the corner shop survive?
items.en: Jamal worries that the new supermarket could take all his customers. Sadia thinks they should focus on what the big store cannot offer. They could deliver within an hour, and they might allow regular customers to pay at the end of the month. Above all, they must keep their friendly service.

units.focus: Talk about possible and imaginary situations in the shop
units.focusBn: দোকানের সম্ভাব্য ও কাল্পনিক পরিস্থিতি নিয়ে কথা বলা

sessions.pattern: If + present, will + verb / If + past, would + verb
sessions.tipBn: বাস্তবে সম্ভব হলে If-এর পরে present আর অন্য অংশে will বসে; কাল্পনিক হলে If-এর পরে past আর অন্য অংশে would বসে।

items.en: If we offer free delivery, more families will order from us.
If you buy two packets, you will get the third one free.
If I had more space, I would sell fresh fish too.
If the supplier comes early, Sadia will stock the shelves before lunch.
If prices kept rising like this, many families would buy less meat.
If I were you, I would compare prices online first.

sessions.pattern: If + don't ..., won't ... / If + didn't ..., wouldn't ...
sessions.tipBn: শর্তবাক্যের যেকোনো অংশে don't, won't, didn't বা wouldn't বসিয়ে না-বোধক করা যায়।

items.en: If you don't keep the receipt, we won't be able to exchange it.
If the card machine doesn't work, customers will have to pay in cash.
If we didn't have online orders, we wouldn't survive this year.
Rahima wouldn't shop anywhere else even if the supermarket were cheaper.
If Nabil doesn't leave now, the frozen food won't stay frozen.
If prices weren't so high, people wouldn't complain so much.

sessions.tipBn: Wh-শব্দ দিয়ে প্রশ্ন শুরু হয়, তারপর will বা would বসে, আর শেষে if-অংশ আসে।

items.en: What will you do if the new supermarket steals your regular customers?
How would you feel if a customer paid with a fake note?
Where will we store the extra rice if the delivery comes today?
Which products would you add if you had a bigger shop?
Who will look after the shop if Jamal goes to his village?
How much would you save if you bought rice by the sack?

sessions.pattern: A short text with first and second conditionals
sessions.tipBn: অনুচ্ছেদে first conditional দিয়ে সম্ভাব্য পরিকল্পনা আর second conditional দিয়ে কাল্পনিক ইচ্ছা বলা হয়।

items.title: Open on Friday mornings
items.en: Sadia has a plan for Friday mornings. If they open at eight, early shoppers will stop by for bread and eggs. If Nabil delivers before Jummah, families won't have to go out in the heat. Jamal says he will try it if Sadia keeps the accounts.

items.title: Jamal's dream
items.en: If Jamal had more money, he would buy the empty shop next door. He would put in a big fridge and sell fresh fish and meat. If the shop were bigger, Rahima could do all her shopping in one place. For now, it is only a dream.

items.title: Rahima's advice
items.en: Rahima often tells young mothers how to shop wisely. If you buy seasonal vegetables, you will save money and eat better. If you shopped once a week instead of every day, you would waste less. And if you are not sure about a price, ask Jamal, because he will always tell you the truth.
